This page covers what is specific to the Smithsonian Hydra cluster. Once you
are set up here, RiboPilot works as in the [Get started](RiboPilot.html)
walkthrough, with `executor = "NMNH_Hydra"`.
[Running on a cluster](Clusters.html) explains how RiboPilot uses a cluster in
general.

You need a Hydra account; see the
[Hydra policies page](https://confluence.si.edu/display/HPC/Hydra+Policies).

# Get an R session on Hydra

The simplest route is the dedicated RStudio Server at
[https://galaxy.si.edu/R4](https://galaxy.si.edu/R4). Log in from a browser
with your Hydra credentials; it can see `/pool`, `/scratch`, and `/store`. It is
a shared resource, so use it for interactive work and submit runs as jobs.
Details are on the
[Hydra RStudio page](https://confluence.si.edu/display/HPC/Dedicated+RStudio+Server).

To run your own RStudio Server session instead, start one on a login node:

```bash
conda deactivate                       # avoid package conflicts
module load tools/R/RStudio/server
start-rstudio-server
```

The command prints an `ssh -N -L ...` line to run in a terminal on your own
computer. Leave both terminals open and open `http://localhost:8787` in a
browser. If port 8787 is taken, pick another with
`start-rstudio-server -port 8890`.

Use Chrome or Firefox, not Safari.

# Install Nextflow

Hydra has no Nextflow module, so install your own copy once. Run these in a
**terminal** on Hydra: an SSH session to a login node, or the Terminal pane of
your RStudio Server session.

```bash
cd ~
module load tools/java/21.0.2
curl -s https://get.nextflow.io | bash
chmod +x nextflow
mkdir -p ~/bin
mv nextflow ~/bin/nextflow
echo 'export PATH="${HOME}/bin:${PATH}"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
```

Job scripts written by the app load Java and read `~/.bashrc` for you. If you
use Nextflow from a shell yourself, run `module load tools/java/21.0.2` first.

# Install RiboPilot

In the R console of your RStudio Server session, follow step 5 of
[Install the tools](Installation.html#install-the-tools). Singularity is
already on Hydra, so there is nothing else to install.

# Create a project

```r
RiboPilot::new_test_project(
  path = "/pool/public/genomics/<USER>/RiboPilot/test_project",
  executor = "NMNH_Hydra"
)
```

Use the same `executor = "NMNH_Hydra"` with `RiboPilot::new_project()` for your
own data. Work under `/pool` or `/scratch`. Home folders are too small, and
projects cannot run from `/store`.

By default Singularity's download cache and the reference folder also sit in
your home folder.
[Disk space, caches, and offline use](Caches-and-Offline.html) shows how to
move them.

# Open the app and run

```r
RiboPilot::RiboPilot("/pool/public/genomics/<USER>/RiboPilot/test_project")
```

An RStudio Server session on Hydra starts without the job scheduler, Java, or
your `~/bin` on its PATH. The app puts them back when it starts. You only need
to call `RiboPilot::hydra_setup()` yourself, once per session, if you run the
pipeline from the R console instead of the app.

Press **Update**. The run window shows a job script that goes to Hydra's queue
for workflow managers. Press **Submit as job**, or **Save script** to submit it
yourself with `qsub`. The job keeps going after you close the browser. Watch it
with `qstat` in a terminal, then press the reload button above the table to see
new results. [Submit a run as a job](Clusters.html#submit-a-run-as-a-job) has
the details.

The [Get started](RiboPilot.html) walkthrough marks each place where Hydra
differs, in boxes tagged HYDRA.
